Coded AI behaviours in human-AI programming sessions

Source: R/data-ai.R
ai_long.Rd

ai_long is a coded dataset, in long format, of the behaviours of an AI coding assistant in "vibe-coding" sessions, in which a person builds software by instructing the assistant in natural language. Each row is one coded AI behaviour, with the project and session it belongs to and its position in the session. A single assistant message can carry several codes, which are ordered within the message.

The log contains 8,551 coded events in 428 sessions from 34 projects. Eight behaviour codes are grouped into three clusters: Action (Delegate, Execute, Investigate), Communication (Ask, Explain, Report) and Repair (Plan, Repair). With session = "session_id", action = "code" and order = "order_in_session", lsa() reads each session as one sequence and tests which behaviour tends to follow which.

Usage

ai_long

Format

A data frame with 8,551 rows (coded events) and 9 columns:

message_id

Integer. Identifier of the assistant message.

project

Character. Project identifier (34 projects).

session_id

Character. Session identifier (428 sessions, each within one project).

timestamp

Integer. Unix time in seconds.

session_date

Character. Session date as YYYY-MM-DD.

code

Character. AI behaviour code (8 values).

cluster

Character. Behaviour cluster (3 values).

code_order

Integer. Position of the code within its message.

order_in_session

Integer. Position of the event within its session.

Source

Taken without modification from Nestimate::ai_long (Nestimate 0.7.7, MIT license).

See also

lsa() and its long-format arguments; group_regulation_long for another event log.

Examples

fit <- lsa(ai_long, session = "session_id", action = "code",
           order = "order_in_session")
transitions(fit, direction = "over", sort = "strength")
